author: LargoScript
description: An optimizing SSA decompiler and live-memory engine for Windows and Linux, PE and ELF alike. Memory-SSA, alias/points-to (stack/global/heap disambiguation), C++ RTTI class recovery (vtable naming, this-typing, template demangling, base-class inheritance graph) and readability structuring that recovers if/else-if/for/while/do-while turn raw x64 into readable, source-level pseudocode; live value/pointer/AOB scanning and hardware watchpoints cover the runtime. One pipeline over static files and live processes — arm a watchpoint on a value and get back the exact decompiled statement that wrote it. Every capability is a stable CLI verb and an MCP tool returning versioned JSON.
name: N0xis

tools.name: annotate_get
tools.description: The current name/type/comment + full history recorded at an address, if any.

tools.name: annotate_list
tools.description: Every annotated address, va-sorted.

tools.name: annotate_set
tools.description: Assert (or clear, with no value) a name/type/comment at an address — the analysis DB, kept as versioned truth: every change is appended to that address's history rather than overwriting it. field is one of "name", "type", or "comment".

value.description: New value; omit to clear the field.

tools.name: attach
tools.description: Attach to a pid or load a static PE file, and record it as the session default in `.n0x/session.json` so later tool calls can omit pid/file. Shared with the CLI (same project directory).

file.description: Path to a PE file to load (static source). Provide exactly one of `pid`/`file`.

pid.description: PID of a running process to attach to (live source).

tools.name: capability_list
tools.description: List every capability this build can run — built-in analysis and user-registered plugins alike, each with its origin and the schema it emits. Read this instead of guessing what exists; a plugin the user registered shows up here exactly like a built-in does.

tools.name: capability_run
tools.description: Run a capability by name (see `capability_list`) with JSON arguments. Target arguments are the usual pid/file/snapshot/remote_cmd/bytes. Dispatching a built-in and dispatching a plugin are the same call — that is the point of the registry.

args.description: Arguments object, passed through to the capability unchanged.

tools.name: decomp_pseudo
tools.description: Decompile a function to pseudo-C. style=ssa (default) is the full path: optimized + structured, and its response includes `delta` — the per-pass optimization log (also available standalone via explain_opt_delta).

explain.description:
Also return the per-round optimization delta (`ssa` style only). Off by
default: measured larger than the pseudocode itself (59% of the
payload). The `ir_opt_delta` tool is the dedicated way to ask for it.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

style.description: One of `"goto"`, `"structured"`, `"ssa"` (default: `"ssa"`, the optimized + structured style).

tools.name: disasm
tools.description: Linear disassembly of `count` instructions starting at `addr`.

addr.description: Address to start disassembling at, e.g. `"0x140001000"`.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Environment / readiness check (arch decoder, project resolution).

tools.name: explain_opt_delta
tools.description: Explain *why* the decompiler produced what it did: runs the same pipeline as decomp_pseudo(style=ssa) and returns only the per-pass optimization delta (n0xis.opt.delta.v1) — copy/const/expr propagation and dead-code elimination, each entry naming the pass, the address, and a summary of what changed.

explain.description:
Also return the per-round optimization delta (`ssa` style only). Off by
default: measured larger than the pseudocode itself (59% of the
payload). The `ir_opt_delta` tool is the dedicated way to ask for it.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

style.description: One of `"goto"`, `"structured"`, `"ssa"` (default: `"ssa"`, the optimized + structured style).

tools.name: function_discover
tools.description: Heuristic function discovery over a code range (defaults to `.text`).

offset.description:
Skip this many candidates before collecting — page through a range
together with `limit`.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

start.description: Start of the scan range; defaults to the module's `.text`.

tools.name: function_trace
tools.description: Call-graph walk (BFS) from a root function address.

addr.description: Root address (or RVA if `addr_rva` is set) to walk the call graph from.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

tools.name: mem_read
tools.description: Read raw bytes from a live process or static file at an address.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

tools.name: mem_write
tools.description: Write raw bytes into a live process's memory at an address.

bytes.description: Space- or contiguous-hex bytes, e.g. `"90 90 C3"` or `"9090C3"`.

pid.description: Live-process only (writing a static file's on-disk bytes isn't a thing).

tools.name: module_list
tools.description: List loaded modules of a live process or a static PE's imports/module table.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

tools.name: plugin_list
tools.description: Every registered analysis plugin (name -> spawn command + declared artifact kinds), from .n0x/plugins.json.

tools.name: plugin_run
tools.description: Manually invoke one registered plugin by name against an arbitrary JSON artifact and return its response. Fails visibly (never panics) if the plugin isn't registered, its command can't spawn, or it crashes/times out — matching PluginHost's own fail-open-but-visible posture.

artifact.description: The artifact JSON to send on the plugin's stdin.

kind.description:
Artifact kind label sent to the plugin alongside `artifact`
(`"cfg"`/`"pseudo"`/`"discover"`, or any caller-chosen string for a
manual test invocation).

tools.name: process_ps
tools.description: List running processes, optionally filtered by name substring.

tools.name: provenance_trace
tools.description: Explain a live memory access: arms a hardware watchpoint on addr, waits for one real hit, then fuses it with the SSA decompiler to resolve the containing function and return the exact decompiled statement responsible — provenance, not just an address.

addr.description: Address of the value to watch.

tools.name: ui_focus
tools.description: Bring a window to the foreground (window selector). NOT read-only — it activates a window on the target. Verifies success via GetForegroundWindow (data.foreground), since the OS often only flashes the taskbar instead of truly focusing.

tools.name: ui_locate
tools.description: Screen region -> memory addresses: hit-test a live target's own UI bounding boxes and report the elements drawing inside a rectangle. Read-only (no breakpoints, no writes). Use `space:"auto"` first and read `observed_range` to learn which coordinate space the target's boxes are in. For noisy results, run once over a rect where the widget is ABSENT with `save_as`, then re-run over the rect where it is PRESENT with `exclude_from` — the spatial diff drops structures that overlap every rect.

align.description: Byte stride between candidate positions (fields are dword-aligned).

exclude_from.description:
Exclude every address found in these previously-saved queries — the
spatial-diff filter (save a rect where the widget is absent, exclude it
from one where it is present).

pid.description:
Live process to hit-test. `ui locate` is live-only: it reads the
target's current retained scene graph.

save_as.description:
Persist this query's addresses under `.n0x/dumps/ui_locate/<name>.json`
so a later query can `exclude_from` it (spatial-diff workflow).

space.description:
`"auto"` (default), `"screen"`, or `"ndc"`. `auto` uses a permissive
bound and reports the observed coordinate range, so you can tell which
space the target's boxes are actually in instead of guessing.

start.description:
Region start (hex). Omit (with `size`) to scan every committed
writable region.

tools.name: ui_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a target window to a PNG so you can visually choose a rect for ui_locate. Read-only-ish (window-dc is fully read-only; printwindow makes the target's UI thread render). CRITICAL: GDI/PrintWindow return an all-black frame for flip-model DirectX windows — this tool detects that and sets data.blank=true with a reason; NEVER treat a blank capture as an empty UI. Key on data.blank, not on ok. Pass out=<path> to write the PNG, base64=true to embed it.

base64.description:
Embed the PNG as base64 in the response. Off by default — a full-window
PNG can be large.

hwnd.description:
Specific window HWND (from `ui_windows`); defaults to the best-guess
game window for the pid.

out.description: Write the PNG here (server-side path). Written even on a blank capture.

tools.name: ui_windows
tools.description: List a target process's top-level windows (title, class, visibility, rects, DPI), best-guess game window first. Read-only. Use it to pick an hwnd for ui_screenshot / ui_focus, or to see why a capture is blank (minimized / cloaked / off-screen). rect_frame is the canonical visible bounds; rect_client is where the game renders.

tools.name: xref
tools.description: Cross-references to (dir=to) or from (dir=from) an address, scanned over a code range.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.

tools.name: xref_string
tools.description: Search a data window for a string literal and find the code that references it (lea xref).

query.description: The string literal to search for.

remote_cmd.description: Attach over a remote transport, e.g. `"ssh host n0xis remote-serve --pid 1234"`.

snapshot.description: Reload a captured `snapshot dump` by name.
